idiom_name: FastAPI routes + Pydantic models (OpenAPI document generated from the code)
implementation_notes: FastAPI is the publication machinery: route decorators declare the protocol surface, Pydantic models are the published language, and the OpenAPI document is derived from those type hints at import time, so the contract cannot drift from the annotations without changing the types. response_model is the translation layer - it filters the response down to the declared schema, so API result objects, dataclasses or ORM entities never serialise directly - and the version is carried by a path prefix (APIRouter(prefix="/v1")) or a header. The framework supplies routing, validation, serialisation and documentation; the parts nobody generates are the decisions about what to expose and the deprecation policy for it.
code_sketch:
router = APIRouter(prefix="/v1")

class OrderAck(BaseModel):                    # the published language
    order_id: str
    status: Literal["ACCEPTED", "REJECTED"]

@router.post("/orders", response_model=OrderAck)          # filters domain fields
async def submit(req: OrderRequest) -> OrderAck:
    return OrderAck.from_domain(orders.submit(req.to_domain()))
pitfalls: Returning a domain object instead of the response_model publishes every attribute, including internal ids and lazily loaded relations.
Optional fields without response_model_exclude_unset/none vary in presence between responses, which clients generated from the document cannot rely on.
The generated document is only as good as the annotations: missing Field(description=...) and example responses yield a valid but useless contract, and a hand-edited openapi.json drifts immediately.
